healthcareSystem: Public healthcare system supplemented by growing private sector. Private hospitals in Dhaka offer adequate care. Public hospitals are overcrowded and under-resourced.
qualityNotes: Private hospitals in Dhaka (Square, United, Apollo) offer reasonable care. Public hospitals are severely overcrowded. English spoken at major private hospitals. For serious conditions, medical evacuation to Bangkok, Singapore, or India is common.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies open daily 8am-10pm in cities. Many 24/7 pharmacies in Dhaka.
pharmacyTips: Lazz Pharma and other pharmacy chains are widespread. Most medications available without prescription at very low prices. Pharmacists may have limited training — self-prescribing is common. Bring your own essential medications to ensure quality.
commonOTC: oral rehydration salts (ORSaline — critical for traveler's diarrhea)
prescriptionRules: Very few prescription requirements in practice. Almost all medications available OTC. Bring essential medications from home for quality assurance.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis/CBD products
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly illegal in Bangladesh. Severe penalties.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English for all prescription medications. Keep in original packaging.

travelInsurance.tips: Travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage is ESSENTIAL. Ensure coverage for evacuation to Bangkok, India, or Singapore for serious conditions.

required: Yellow fever (if arriving from an endemic area)
vaccinations.notes: Yellow fever certificate required from endemic countries. Cholera and traveler's diarrhea are significant risks. Malaria risk in some border areas — consult a travel doctor.

waterNotes: Do NOT drink tap water. Use bottled water only. Avoid ice in drinks. Use bottled water for brushing teeth. Arsenic contamination affects some groundwater sources in rural areas.
foodSafetyTips: Eat freshly cooked, hot food only. Avoid raw vegetables, salads, and unpeeled fruit. Street food should be piping hot. Biryani and curries from busy restaurants are generally safe. Avoid buffets that have been sitting.
medicalTourismNote: Bangladesh is not a medical tourism destination. Many Bangladeshis travel to India, Thailand, or Singapore for advanced medical care.
metaDescription: Travel health guide for Bangladesh, emergency 999, Cannabis banned, limited public healthcare. Hospital info, pharmacy tips, vaccinations, and travel insurance.

hospitals.name: Square Hospital
hospitals.notes: Leading private hospital. Modern facilities. English-speaking doctors. 24/7 emergency.

hospitals.name: United Hospital
hospitals.notes: Modern private hospital in expat area. Good for tourist medical needs.

hospitals.name: Apollo Hospital Dhaka
hospitals.notes: Part of Apollo international chain. International patient services.

pharmacyPhrases.english: I need medicine for a headache

dentalCare.availability: Dental care available in Dhaka at private clinics. Quality varies.
dentalCare.notes: Private dental clinics in Dhaka's Gulshan and Banani areas serve international patients. Basic care is affordable.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Square Hospital and United Hospital have dental departments for emergencies.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Limited. Some available through private hospitals in Dhaka.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are limited. English-speaking support mainly available through private hospitals and expatriate networks.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is very limited in Bangladesh. Sidewalks, buildings, and transport are generally not accessible.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Major private hospitals have some accessibility. Public hospitals have very limited access.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Rickshaws and private cars are the main options. Traffic congestion in Dhaka is extreme.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Bangladesh is very challenging for travelers with mobility limitations. Plan all logistics carefully. Use private transport and contact hotels/tour operators in advance about specific needs.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: No formal requirements but masks may be recommended in crowded areas.
covidStatus.testing: Tests available at private hospitals and clinics in Dhaka.
covidStatus.notes: Bangladesh has lifted most COVID restrictions.

insuranceClaimProcess: Private hospitals provide English-language documentation and receipts. Keep all records. Medical evacuation to India or Thailand is common — ensure your insurer is notified promptly. File claims within 30 days.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs at private or international facilities. Public-system rates can be much lower (or free for residents). Actual costs vary by city, facility, and exchange rate.

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation insurance is essential for serious cases. Singapore and Bangkok are the regional medical hubs. Indian metros (Mumbai, Delhi) handle complex cases for the subcontinent. Actual costs depend on distance, aircraft type, and whether ICU-level care is required in transit.

drugNameMap.note: Crocin (GSK) is the dominant Indian-subcontinent brand. Calpol is for kids.
Brufen (Abbott) is the most common; Combiflam is paracetamol+ibuprofen combo.
